correctness.rationale: With common sum s, let Δ be the second product minus the first. The second and third differences are 2Δ and 3sΔ. Their vanishing implies 2Δ=sΔ=0 (subtract s times the second equation), and the pair-power recurrence P_j=sP_{j−1}−uP_{j−2}, P_0=2, P_1=s, then implies ΔP_j=0 for every j for either product u. Subtracting the two recurrences now proves closure at all degrees. With z=x−a,w=x−b,y=x−a−b, Δ=ab and s=2x−a−b. At odd p the count for the product condition is p^k+k(p−1)p^{k−1}: a=0 contributes p^k and each of k finite valuation classes contributes (p−1)p^{k−1}. At 2^k, k≥2, the zero-product count is (k+2)2^{k−1} and a displacement 2^{k−1} is admissible exactly for the k−2 ordered positive valuation splits summing to k−1, each contributing 2^{k−1}. Multiply by the independent p^k choices of x; at 2 all powers are the first power, giving 8, and the residue singleton gives 1. CRT multiplies exact local counts. The first-sum-only example differs by 2 in its second sum for N>2; the stated a=1,b=N/2 example has agreement at degree two but difference N/2 at degree three when 4|N.
